rules.rule: Make the headline specific enough that a stranger with zero context understands the niche and promise instantly.

rules.rule: Keep the About body focused on outcome and inside Skool's 1,000-character hard cap (aim for 900-985 so nothing gets cut).
rules.check: Count the About body's characters including emojis and line breaks. Over 1,000 fails outright; anything padded with topic rambling instead of outcome language also fails even under the cap.
rules.why: 1,000 characters is Skool's actual limit on the About body, not a style suggestion. A page that reads like 500 words of prose is already over the real ceiling before anyone judges the writing.

rules.rule: State clearly who the community is for and what shared goal members have.
rules.check: Check for an explicit sentence naming the target member and their shared objective.
rules.why: A page that never names its reader can't make that reader feel seen.

rules.rule: Use specific, concrete pain points and benefits instead of generic promises.
rules.check: Check whether benefit statements name a real, specific problem or number rather than vague uplift language.
rules.why: Specificity is what makes copy believable and self-selecting.

rules.rule: Share one personal credibility line or real setback, not a full background or biography section.

rules.rule: Make the first line of the About body work as a headline a stranger can quote back, since it is the only bold-able line.
rules.check: Read the first line of the body; if it is a greeting, a warning, or a trial notice instead of the outcome, it fails.
rules.why: The first line is what shows above the fold beside the video.

rules.rule: Keep the sidebar headline (group description) under Skool's 150-character hard cap, aiming for 130-148 so nothing truncates.
rules.check: Count the headline's characters including emojis and spaces. Over 150 fails; a headline that only just squeaks under 150 by dropping the outcome also fails.
rules.why: 150 characters is Skool's real limit on the sidebar line, not a style guess; a punchy outcome has to fit inside it or it gets cut off mid-sentence.

rules.rule: Never use Skool's banned empty-AI phrases: "No fluff, just results," "Remove the guesswork," "Stop overthinking," "You don't need more ___, you need to know what actually works."
rules.check: Grep the body for these phrases or close paraphrases of them; any match fails.
rules.why: Skool's own classroom lesson flags these exact lines as meaningless filler that reads as generic, not as a promise.

rules.rule: Do not include your background or biography on the About page.
rules.check: Check for a standalone paragraph about the creator's history, career, or credentials that isn't in service of a single proof line (see R55).
rules.why: The lesson names biography explicitly as something that does not belong on the page; readers came for the outcome, not the founder's resume.

rules.rule: Once you have a real testimonial or member win, put it in an attachment slot as a screenshot of the actual post or review.
rules.check: Check whether any attachment shows a real testimonial, review, or member win; a page with reviews available but none surfaced fails.
rules.why: A screenshotted win from inside the community is more convincing proof than a designed testimonial graphic or none at all.

sources.speaker: Skool team
sources.video_title: How To Grow Your Skool | Skool News #24

rules.rule: Structure the VSL as promise, pain, proof, what's inside, objections, urgency, then a direct call to action.
rules.check: Watch the video and check whether it hits, in roughly this order: what it teaches, the viewer's frustration, evidence it works, what's inside, the top objections answered, a reason to act now, and a plain 'join' ask.
rules.why: This is Skool's own tested VSL structure; skipping a beat (objections especially) leaves a doubt the video never answers.

rules.rule: Keep the VSL to 2-5 minutes and put enough of the hook in the first 30-40 seconds to hold a distracted viewer.
rules.check: Check the video's runtime and whether the promise or pain point is stated before the 40-second mark; a slow open or a video over 5 minutes fails.
rules.why: Cold traffic decides fast; a video that rambles before it gets to the point loses the viewer before the pitch starts.

rules.rule: Order attachments by proof: the VSL first, the strongest social proof second, then process or mechanism shots after.
rules.check: Check the attachment sequence; a page that leads with a weak or generic image before the VSL, or buries its best proof at the end, fails.
rules.why: Visitors scroll attachments in order, so the strongest evidence has to front-load the sequence, not trail it.

rules.rule: Give each attachment image one idea, not a compound slide trying to make several points at once.
rules.check: Check whether any single attachment stacks multiple unrelated claims or visuals; a slide doing double duty fails.
rules.why: One idea per image is scannable in a half-second scroll; a crowded slide asks the viewer to stop and parse it.

rules.rule: Do not include an attachment that only restates the cover image's message.
rules.check: Compare each attachment's core message to the cover image; any attachment saying the same thing with no new proof or detail fails.
rules.why: A repeat slide spends one of six scarce slots without adding anything a visitor hasn't already seen.

rules.rule: Cut any attachment slot that doesn't earn its place; do not fill all six slots by default.
rules.check: Check whether every attachment adds a distinct, load-bearing piece of proof or information; an attachment kept only because the slot exists fails.
rules.why: Having six slots available is not a requirement to use six; a weak filler image dilutes the stronger ones around it.

rules.rule: Make sure any text inside an attachment image is legible on a mobile screen.
rules.check: Zoom the attachment to roughly a phone's on-screen size; text that's illegible or requires zooming to read fails.
rules.why: Most About-page traffic is mobile, and text too small to read on a phone might as well not be there.

rules.rule: Use high-resolution, high-fidelity images and video in every attachment; no visible compression artifacts or blur.
rules.check: Zoom into each attachment; visible pixelation, blur, or resolution mismatch fails.
rules.why: A blurry or low-fidelity image undercuts credibility even when the message itself is right.

rules.rule: Before you have real reviews or testimonials, leave that slot empty rather than faking or padding it.
rules.check: Check whether a testimonial-shaped attachment actually contains a genuine review; a placeholder, stock quote, or restated cover image standing in for proof fails.
rules.why: A fake or generic stand-in reads worse than no slot at all, and it's easy to add the real thing once it exists.

rules.rule: Show the actual person and the outcome together in at least one attachment, not only text or product graphics.
rules.check: Check whether at least one attachment shows a real person doing the activity or living the outcome the community teaches.
rules.why: A concrete person-plus-outcome image communicates the promise faster than a bullet list or an abstract graphic.

rules.rule: Compact the body for mobile: cut hard line breaks between sections and drop items every Skool member already expects (chat, ask-me-anything access).
rules.check: Check for excess blank-line spacing between sections and for bullets restating platform-default features rather than this community's specifics.
rules.why: Extra whitespace and generic bullets burn scroll distance on a small screen without adding information.

rules.rule: Avoid the fire, crown, gem, and shamrock emojis in copy or cover text; they read as Skool's own streak and level icons and confuse the message.
rules.check: Scan the cover image, headline, and body for these four emojis; any use fails, unless one is being consciously repurposed for a matching literal meaning (e.g. fire for an actual cooking niche).
rules.why: Those emojis carry a specific platform meaning on Skool (streaks, levels), so reusing them for something else muddies the promise.

note: Only surfaces a creator can edit: display name, sidebar headline (metadata.description, 150-character hard cap), About body (lpDescription, unicode bold allowed, 1,000-character hard cap), cover image, up to six About attachments (video/images). Skool UI, buttons, pricing tiers, trial, reviews-as-a-feature, levels, and join questions are product and are never graded.
